predecessors.note: The infobox lists the British Military Administration as predecessor; the Allied administration ran 'from 13 May 1943 until Libyan independence was granted in 1951' (Allied occupation of Libya page); the Emirate page gives no dates for the administration.

successors.note: 'The independence of the Kingdom of Libya was declared on 24 December 1951'; the infobox dates the joining of Tripolitania and Fezzan-Ghadames to form the kingdom to the same day.

capitals.name: Benghazi
capitals.note: Idris proclaimed himself Emir at a 'national conference' in Benghazi; infobox capital Benghazi.

rulers.name: Idris (Sayyid Idris al-Senussi)
rulers.title: Emir of Cyrenaica
rulers.note: He 'proclaimed himself Emir of Cyrenaica'; he became King of Libya on 24 December 1951.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1949-1951 (no Cliopatria row): the emirate is read as the historic region Cyrenaica, the province of the later kingdom (850,000 km2 on the Kingdom of Libya page); the Emirate page gives no area or boundary. Cliopatria draws no polity for Libya between 1943 (Italian Africa) and 1953 (Kingdom of Libya).

ledger.note: 1949: Idris proclaims the Emirate of Cyrenaica at Benghazi. He 'unilaterally proclaimed Cyrenaica an independent Senussi emirate on 1 March 1949' (the page gives 1 March, not 1 June); the United Kingdom backed it, but the United Nations on 21 November 1949 directed Britain and France to prepare Libya's independence.

1951: the emirate becomes a province of the Kingdom of Libya on 24 December. 'The independence of the Kingdom of Libya was declared on 24 December 1951'; the infobox dates the joining of Tripolitania and Fezzan-Ghadames to form the kingdom to the same day.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; the emirate is the historic region Cyrenaica, whose limits with Tripolitania and the Egyptian frontier are approximate.

sources.title: Emirate of Cyrenaica
sources.note: Proclaimed 1 March 1949 by Idris in Benghazi; British backing; the UN directive of 21 November 1949; merged into the Kingdom of Libya on 24 December 1951.

sources.title: Kingdom of Libya
sources.note: Predecessors of the kingdom, the three provinces and their areas (Cyrenaica 850,000 km2), independence 24 December 1951.

sources.title: Allied occupation of Libya
sources.note: British administration of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica from 13 May 1943 to 1951.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks, written as a direct predecessor of kingdom-of-libya (af-08-e) from the pages opened for that dossier. The Emirate page gives no area, boundary or dates for the preceding British Military Administration, and describes no protectorate or treaty with Britain, only British backing; the page's date of 1 March 1949 is used. Tripolitania under the British Military Administration (1943-1951) and Fezzan-Ghadames under French administration have no dossier; Cliopatria's Libya row begins in 1953.
